description: Per-filter latency derived from trace spans. Tempo's metrics-generator turns every span into RED metrics; praxis emits one span per filter per phase, so span_name is the breakdown key. This answers 'which filter costs what', which a trace waterfall can only show one request at a time.

panels.description: Tail latency per filter span across the window, worst first in the legend table. Praxis emits one span per filter per phase, so `span_name` (`filter:<name>:<phase>`) is the breakdown key — this is the per-filter cost question answered as a query rather than by eyeballing a waterfall. Phases matter: `:request` runs before the upstream call, `:response` on headers, `:response_body` only when a body is actually inspected. **SAMPLED plane** — percentiles are unbiased under random sampling, volumes are not. Source: `histogram_quantile(0.99, traces_spanmetrics_latency_bucket)`, top 12 spans.

defaults.noValue: No span metrics yet - see the dashboard description

panels.title: P99 Latency by Filter Span

panels.description: Median latency per filter span, to be read against the P99 panel directly above. A filter with a low median and a high P99 is **bursty** — occasional slow calls, typically I/O or a lock — while one where the two are close is uniformly expensive and is a better optimisation target. **SAMPLED plane**: distributions are valid, volume is not. Source: `histogram_quantile(0.50, traces_spanmetrics_latency_bucket)`, top 12 spans.
panels.title: P50 Latency by Filter Span

panels.description: Total time per second attributable to each filter, which reorders the ranking against raw P99: a fast filter that runs on every request can cost more wall clock than a slow one that rarely fires. Deliberately mixes planes — the quantile is from **sampled** span metrics (valid under sampling), the request rate from `praxis_http_requests_total`, a Prometheus counter covering **100%** of requests. Using the span-derived call rate here instead would under-report by exactly the sampling factor while looking entirely plausible.
panels.title: Weighted Filter Cost (sampled P99 x true request rate)

panels.description: How often each span is produced per second — the shape of the filter chain rather than its cost. Request-phase spans run once per request, so they should all sit at roughly the same rate; a `:response_body` span sitting materially lower means that filter only inspects some responses. **SAMPLED plane, so these are not true request counts** — they are low by the sampling factor. Read absolute volume from `praxis_http_requests_total` instead; use this panel for relative shape only.
panels.title: Span Rate by Filter

panels.description: P50 and P99 of the trace root span — the whole request through the gateway, including the upstream model call — for scale against the per-filter panels above. Against a real model this is dominated by inference: if the root is hundreds of milliseconds while every `filter:*` span is sub-millisecond, the gateway is not the bottleneck and the filter chain's total overhead is the sum of those small spans. **SAMPLED plane.** Source: `traces_spanmetrics_latency_bucket` filtered to `span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER"`, which selects the root.
panels.title: End-to-End Request Latency (from spans)

panels.description: Spans that recorded an error status, per second, broken out by which filter produced them — this localises a failure to a specific filter and phase instead of just telling you the request failed. Empty ("No errors") is the healthy state and is what this demo normally shows. Note a 429 from the token budget is a deliberate admission decision, **not** a span error, so rate-limited requests do not appear here — look at Admitted vs Denied for those. **SAMPLED plane**: an error on an unsampled request leaves no span behind, so this under-reports whenever sampling is below 1.0.
panels.title: Span Errors
